questions.question_text:
The vectors $\begin{pmatrix}m\\8\end{pmatrix}$ and $\begin{pmatrix}3\\-6\end{pmatrix}$ are perpendicular.
Find the value of $m$.

options.why: Solved $3m=-48$; moving $-48$ to the other side makes it $+48$.
Stopped at $3m=48$ without dividing by $3$.
Divided $48$ by the $8$ from the vector instead of by the coefficient $3$.

questions.question_text:
The vectors $4\underset{\sim}{i}-9\underset{\sim}{j}$ and $k\underset{\sim}{i}+8\underset{\sim}{j}$ are perpendicular.
Find the value of $k$.

options.why: Dropped the negative sign in $(-9)(8)$, obtaining $4k+72=0$.
Stopped at $4k=72$ without dividing by $4$.
Divided $72$ by $9$ instead of by the coefficient $4$.

questions.question_text:
The points $A(2,-3)$, $B(7,1)$ and $C(3,6)$ are given.
Is $\angle ABC$ a right angle?

options.why: Tested the angle at $A$ instead of at $B$; both vectors must start at the vertex being tested.
Made both products positive, using $20+20$ instead of $20-20$.

options.text: Yes, because $\overrightarrow{BA}$ and $\overrightarrow{BC}$ have equal magnitudes
options.why: Equal side lengths make the triangle isosceles; only a zero dot product shows a right angle.

questions.solution_text:
$\overrightarrow{BA}=(2-7,\,-3-1)=\begin{pmatrix}-5\\-4\end{pmatrix}$
$\overrightarrow{BC}=(3-7,\,6-1)=\begin{pmatrix}-4\\5\end{pmatrix}$
$\overrightarrow{BA}\cdot\overrightarrow{BC}$
$=(-5)(-4)+(-4)(5)$
$=20-20$
$=0$
The dot product is zero, so $\angle ABC=90^{\circ}$.

questions.question_text: Find all values of $n$ for which $\begin{pmatrix}n\\3\end{pmatrix}$ and $\begin{pmatrix}n+2\\-5\end{pmatrix}$ are perpendicular.

options.why: Sign slip when factorising $n^{2}+2n-15$ as $(n+3)(n-5)$.
Solved $n^{2}+2n=0$, dropping the $-15$ from $(3)(-5)$.
Gave only one root; the quadratic here has two valid solutions.

questions.question_text: Find all values of $q$ for which $\begin{pmatrix}q\\3\end{pmatrix}$ and $\begin{pmatrix}q+4\\-4\end{pmatrix}$ are perpendicular.

options.why: Factorised $q^{2}+4q-12$ incorrectly as $(q+2)(q-6)$, which has middle term $-4q$.
Omitted $(3)(-4)=-12$ and solved $q(q+4)=0$.
Kept only the root from $q-2=0$ and omitted the valid root from $q+6=0$.

questions.solution_text:
$(q)(q+4)+(3)(-4)=0$
$q^{2}+4q-12=0$
$(q-2)(q+6)=0$
$q=2$ or $q=-6$
Neither value makes either vector zero, so both are valid.

questions.question_text: For which values of $t$ are $\underset{\sim}{u}=\begin{pmatrix}t+1\\t+1\end{pmatrix}$ and $\underset{\sim}{v}=\begin{pmatrix}t\\5\end{pmatrix}$ perpendicular?

options.why: Kept $t=-1$, which makes $\underset{\sim}{u}$ the zero vector; the zero vector has no direction, so the test does not apply.
Rejected the wrong root; it is $t=-1$ that makes $\underset{\sim}{u}$ the zero vector.
Sign slip when solving $(t+1)(t+5)=0$; the roots of $(t+1)(t+5)$ are negative.

questions.solution_text:
$(t+1)(t)+(t+1)(5)=0$
$(t+1)(t+5)=0$
$t=-1$ or $t=-5$
When $t=-1$, $\underset{\sim}{u}=\begin{pmatrix}0\\0\end{pmatrix}$, which has no direction and so cannot be perpendicular to $\underset{\sim}{v}$.
$t=-5$

questions.question_text:
The vectors $\begin{pmatrix}x\\7\end{pmatrix}$ and $\begin{pmatrix}4\\-4\end{pmatrix}$ are perpendicular.
The value of $x$ is...

options.why: Dropped the negative sign in $(7)(-4)$ and solved $4x+28=0$.
Stopped at $4x=28$ without dividing by $4$.
Divided $28$ by the component $7$ instead of by the coefficient $4$.

questions.solution_text: Perpendicular vectors have zero dot product: $(x)(4)+(7)(-4)=0$. Thus $4x-28=0$, so $4x=28$ and $x=7$.

questions.question_text: If $\mathbf{u}=\begin{pmatrix}-3\\2\end{pmatrix}$ and $\mathbf{v}=\begin{pmatrix}1\\t\end{pmatrix}$ are perpendicular, what is the value of $t$?

options.why: Moved $-3$ across the equals sign without changing its sign, obtaining $2t=-3$.
Stopped at $2t=3$ without dividing by $2$.
Reversed the division in $2t=3$, calculating $2\div3$ instead of $3\div2$.

questions.solution_text: Perpendicular vectors have dot product zero: $(-3)(1)+(2)(t)=-3+2t=0$. Hence $2t=3$ and $t=\frac{3}{2}$.
